neighbours.label: An inflectional suffix piece split from a capitalized stem (Settlement|s, London|ers, Berlin|ers, Bright|en, Tight|en); the same words as single tokens do not fire
fire: Many Berliners spend their summer weekends at the lakes.
Loyal Dubliners still argue about the best pub in the city.
The Highlanders marched south in the autumn of 1745.
Some Westerners find the custom hard to understand.
Select Brighten from the menu to lift the shadows.
Use the Tighten setting before you export the image.
The Lengthen option stretches the clip without changing its pitch.

quiet: Many tourists spend their summer weekends at the beach.
Recent payments to the supplier were summarised in the report.
The governments of both countries signed the treaty.
Several departments share the same building.
Please tighten the bolts before you ride.
You can sharpen the image before you export it.
The Statements were filed with the court on Monday.
The Elements of Style is still widely read.

predictions: Capitalized words that split into stem + -s/-ers/-en/-ments reach 0.4-0.75 on the suffix piece. Capitalized or lowercase words the tokenizer keeps whole (payments, governments, tighten, sharpen, Statements, Elements) stay under 0.15; the broad flag (2.4% of tokens above 0.1 of max) means near misses will not be silent.
short: suffix piece after a capitalized stem
notes: Probe: Londoners 0.733 ('ers'), Straighten 0.710 ('en'), Settlements 0.647 ('s'), lowercase straighten 0.403, all-caps PERMISSIONS 0.142 ('S'); single-token settlements 0.072, exports 0.036, Parisians 0.038, cat floor 0.135. Card: 'en' x7, 'ín' x5, 'S' x4, 's', 'ers', ' Station' peaks on Settlement|s, London|ers, Straight|en, Ste|en, EXPORT|S (max 1.14, layer 2, broad). A layer-2 pole that marks a suffix continuing a capitalized stem; lowercase splits fire more weakly and are kept out of both halves.
